messages:
owen: Thinking about adding A10/T4 mixes to our spot pools in us-west-2 to cut costs. Main concerns: bin-packing efficiency across different GPU sizes, cross-AZ network perf, and interruption/fallback priorities. Anyone tried an AZ-aware mixed pool recently?

maria: We ran a small run last month. A10s give decent throughput for medium models but lower FP16 perf vs A100. T4s are fine for short contexts, but long-context workloads tank.

chen: For our LLMs, p99 latency went up ~15% with T4s when using the same batch config. Cost/token was ~40% lower. Good tradeoff for async embedding/sync background jobs, not for low-latency chat.

owen: @maria can you paste the placement policy you used?

maria: Sure — simplified version of the node group policy we tested:
```yaml
nodeGroupSelector:
  - instanceTypes: [a2-highgpu-1g, a10g, nvidia-tesla-t4]
  - prefer: [a2-highgpu-1g] # prefer high perf first
  - binpackBy: [gpu_mem, cpu] # pack like-memory GPUs together
  - fallbackOrder: [a2-highgpu-1g, a10g, t4]
  - azAffinityCooldown: 600 # seconds to avoid rapid rebalance
```

chen: Important note — us-west-2a had near-zero availability for a2 instances during the test window. We added AZ-affinity with a short cooldown which reduced flapping.

owen: How are we handling preempt signals and checkpoints? Need <30s resume for hot routes.

maria: We used incremental KV-checkpointing + S3 multipart. Handler on node: `trap 'upload_ckpt.sh' SIGTERM` then small flush of last 2 minibatches. Combined with quick restart it gave ~25s resume in practice.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling update started for spot-pool-mix experiment at 2026-02-12T10:02Z

owen: Any cross-AZ networking issues when A10/T4 pods talk to p4d shards?

chen: Cross-AZ adds ~1–3ms tail on KV fetches, p99 increased ~2ms. Mitigation: colocate KV cache with model shards when possible, use NLB with TCP keepalive tweaks, and prefer same-AZ binpacking for latency-sensitive routes.

maria: Also worth doing size-aware binpacking: try to pack GPUs of similar memory/compute together so batch shapes are homogeneous — reduces padding waste and keeps throughput predictable.

owen: Proposed policy: pin hot/low-latency routes to A100/p4d where possible; allow cheaper A10/T4 mix for background/async and overflow capacity. Make routing decisions by route SLA and cost budget.

chen: +1. Let's run a week-long canary: 20% of capacity to A10/T4 mix, monitor p95/p99 and cost_per_token. I can stand up a dashboard.

owen: Created dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/spot-mix-experiment (will share read-only link to infra team)

maria: Notes: ensure regional quotas across AZs before rollout, and set an eviction buffer of +5% so we don't run into cold-start cascades when spot capacity shrinks.

owen: Ok scheduling canary and will add azAffinityCooldown and checkpoint handler to the nodegroup bootstrap. Thanks all :rocket:
